title: Mittal-Backed Consortium in Talks for Liverpool Stake at $6 Billion Valuation
excerpt: Amit Bhatia's group, backed by steel tycoon Lakshmi Mittal's family and potentially Jeff Bezos, is pursuing a 30% minority stake in one of football's most valuable clubs.
body:
• Amit Bhatia's consortium is negotiating to acquire a 30% stake in Liverpool FC, valuing the club at $6 billion.
  • Jeff Bezos has been approached to join the investment group but has not confirmed his involvement.
  • Fenway Sports Group's potential sale would represent a fifteenfold increase from their 2010 purchase price of £300 million.
  • Bhatia has transferred his stake in QPR to focus on the Liverpool investment, indicating his commitment to the deal.
Key Takeaways
  • Amit Bhatia's consortium seeks a 30% stake in Liverpool FC, valuing the club at $6 billion.
  • Jeff Bezos has been approached to join the investment group but hasn't confirmed his participation.
  • Bhatia transferred his QPR stake to facilitate the Liverpool investment, emphasizing his commitment.
  • FSG's potential sale represents a fifteenfold increase from their 2010 purchase price of £300 million.

Fenway Sports Group is in talks to sell a significant minority stake in Liverpool Football Club to a consortium led by Amit Bhatia and backed by the Mittal family, in a deal that would value the six-time European champions at more than $6 billion, according to the Financial Times.

https://x.com/centregoals/status/2079587036625854692

FSG confirmed the negotiations, telling Sky Sports News: "An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

The proposed stake could be as large as 30%, according to journalist Ben Jacobs, translating to a purchase price of approximately £1.35 billion. Talks have been ongoing for three months, the Guardian reported, suggesting this is a serious, structured process rather than a speculative approach.

The Consortium: Bhatia, Mittal, and Potentially Bezos

Bhatia, 46, is an investment banker-turned-entrepreneur with experience in football ownership. He served as co-owner of Queens Park Rangers in the English Championship, where he oversaw the club's promotion to the Premier League in 2011. He transferred his QPR stake to majority owner Ruben Gnanalingam on July 21, clearing the path for the Liverpool bid.

The financial firepower behind the consortium comes from Bhatia's father-in-law, Lakshmi Mittal, the Luxembourg-based steel magnate whose family fortune Forbes estimates at more than £22 billion. The Mittal family is no stranger to sports ownership, having acquired a majority stake in Indian Premier League franchise Rajasthan Royals in May 2026.

In a development that could add another dimension to the deal, Sky News reported Wednesday that Amazon founder Jeff Bezos — the world's fourth-richest person with an estimated $257 billion fortune — has been approached about joining the consortium. A source cautioned that Bezos was not certain to proceed. He has previously explored bids for NFL teams the Seattle Seahawks and Washington Commanders without finalizing either deal.

![Jeff Bezos. Jeff Bezos has been approached to join the investment group but hasn't confirmed his participation.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fc/260202-D-PM193-2205_SECWAR_Arsenal_of_Freedom_Tour_-_Florida_%283x4_cropped_on_Bezos_and_rotated%29.jpg)

A Fifteenfold Return for FSG

The $6 billion valuation underscores the spiraling value of elite Premier League assets. FSG, controlled by American billionaire John W. Henry, bought Liverpool for £300 million in 2010 when the club was on the brink of administration. The proposed deal would represent a fifteenfold increase in that purchase price over 16 years.

"This is such a robust and premium asset in the market that there is no question that it is a fantastic potential investment."

— Amber Pinto, Financial Analyst

This is not FSG's first minority sale. In 2023, the group sold a roughly 4% stake to US private equity firm Dynasty Equity for up to $200 million — a passive investment that was not used to fund transfers. The Bhatia deal would be "much larger, potentially 30%, and it will inevitably fuel speculation that in the coming years FSG will look to exit Liverpool," said Sky News business editor Mark Kleinman.

FSG insists the deal does not signal a full sale. Sources described it as a way to inject capital into the club rather than a step toward relinquishing control.

Indian Capital in Global Football

The Mittal-backed bid represents the latest — and potentially largest — entry of Indian capital into top-tier European football. While Indian business families have invested across cricket, kabaddi, and other domestic sports, the Premier League has remained largely the domain of American, Gulf, and Southeast Asian investors.

The deal would place the Mittal family alongside the most prominent club owners in world football. The $6 billion valuation broadly matches the $6.3 billion at which Sir Jim Ratcliffe's minority stake valued Manchester United in 2023, and dwarfs the $3.3 billion Chelsea sale to the Clearlake-Boehly consortium.

What It Means for Liverpool on the Pitch

Liverpool enter a period of transition this summer. Head coach Arne Slot was sacked after winning the Premier League title the season before last and replaced by Andoni Iraola. Michael Edwards, the influential chief executive of football for FSG, departed this month in what the group called a "planned transition."

Investment Landscape in Football
›Indian capital enters top-tier European football.
›Valuation aligns with Manchester United's minority stake.
›Dwarfs Chelsea's sale to Clearlake-Boehly consortium.

Financial analyst Amber Pinto cautioned that a minority stake would not necessarily translate into immediate transfer spending. "A deal this size won't be done over a short time frame," she said. "This could lead to growth and increases in revenue that could impact the budget" — but the path runs through commercial expansion rather than direct capital injection into the squad.

Football finance expert Kieran Maguire offered a blunter assessment: "FSG are very cold, very ruthless and very forensic in terms of their analysis. The continued investment in Liverpool is not done for reasons of affection."
